citations.narrative:
While reviewing disposition paperwork and discussing animals that are no longer at the facility the licensee stated that
one of the coatimundis had escaped the facility and had not been recovered.
On July 7th 2026 the licensee removed both coatimundis from their enclosure to provide them with opportunities for
enrichment, which is routinely done at this facility. There was a loud noise that startled the female coatimundi and she
escaped through an open door and ran into an adjacent field. The licensee attempted to recapture the coatimundi through
verbal commands and using food rewards but was unsuccessful. At the time of inspection the coatimundi has not been
captured and has not been seen.
Failure to handle animals carefully and in way that keeps them contained can leave the animals exposed to weather
extremes, predation, and injury. The licensee must handle all animals carefully and in a manner that does not cause
trauma, overheating, excessive cooling, stress, physical harm, and unnecessary discomfort.
To be corrected from this point forward on 10-20-26.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
